answer.headline: No anomalous year-over-year passenger months at MIA, January 2024–June 2026
answer.body: The time-series anomaly screen on monthly enplaned passengers at Miami International Airport (MIA) flagged no month from January 2024 through June 2026. The screen scores each month year-over-year change against MIA own year-over-year history using a robust z-score, at the catalog default threshold. Months in 2024 are the comparison baseline and are not scored, because this passenger series begins in January 2024. Observed enplanements run from {F32} in January 2024 to {F61} in June 2026. June 2026 was {F63} versus June 2025 (calculated). A descriptive linear fit over the same monthly series slopes at {F62} (calculated); that slope includes seasonality and is not an anomaly flag.

claims.text: Monthly enplaned passengers at MIA are observed from January 2024 ({F32}) through June 2026 ({F61}). The trend window covering those months is {F62.period}.
June 2026 enplanements ({F61}, observed) were {F63} versus June 2025 ({F49}, observed). This year-over-year change is calculated for the last month of the window and is not an anomaly flag.

On this same monthly series, the time-series anomaly screen returned no flagged months, so no scored month had a year-over-year change that was unusual relative to MIA own year-over-year history under the default robust-z rule.

assumptions: MIA is Miami International Airport in Miami, FL, the unique airport resolved from that name and code.

An anomaly here means the catalog time-series screen: a robust z-score of the monthly year-over-year change in enplaned passengers versus the airport own history, at the default threshold. It is not a cross-airport outlier test and not a judgment about demand, capacity, or operations.
limitations: The screen flags unusual year-over-year changes and does not identify causes.
Calendar 2024 cannot be tested for a year-over-year anomaly because there is no earlier year in this passenger series.
A seasonal level that repeats is not flagged when the prior year was similar. The test is on the change, not the level.
Unmet demand, terminal capacity, fares, and profitability are not measured by these data.
The screen emits a finding only for a flagged month, so the empty result is the operator output rather than a stored count of anomalies.
Passenger coverage in this catalog extends through July 2026; July 2026 was outside the requested window and was not screened.
